answer: Reputation-Weighted Work Ledger. Each agent must forge a signed history of completed tasks before its outputs count toward payouts. New clones start with zero verified history, so they earn nothing until they perform and get counter-verified work—costing real compute and time per identity. Honest agents reuse one ledger, making honesty cheaper than cloning. A zephyr of fresh identities gains no advantage; each still needs a quill of recorded, checked labor before earning. Attackers pay full task cost per clone with no shortcut.
